entries.core_move: Convert a cosine A cos($\omega$ t + $\phi$) into the phasor A angle $\phi$, preserving amplitude and phase for same-frequency phasor addition.
Add same-frequency cosines by recognizing their common angular frequency, converting each cosine to its phasor, and summing the phasors as complex quantities.

entries.lesson_title: Rectangular Form of a Phasor Sum
entries.core_move: Compute the rectangular-form phasor sum for same-frequency cosines by resolving each phasor into real and imaginary components and adding corresponding components.

entries.lesson_title: Polar Form of a Phasor Sum
entries.core_move: Convert a rectangular phasor sum into polar magnitude-angle form so the resultant sinusoid's amplitude and phase can be read from the phasor.

entries.lesson_title: Converting a Phasor Sum Back to a Sinusoid
entries.core_move: Convert a polar phasor sum back into a single same-frequency sinusoid by mapping magnitude to amplitude and angle to phase at the common angular frequency.

entries.lesson_title: Amplitude-Phase Form of a Sinusoidal Sum
entries.core_move: Express a same-frequency sinusoidal sum in amplitude-phase form by adding component phasors and converting the resultant magnitude and angle into the combined amplitude and phase.
